## Signature

`docker/qemu/run-aarch64-boot-test-strict.sh`, run 2 of 3 twenty-boot runs
during the #822 landing re-smoke at merged head `ab1df542` (2026-09-06, Apple
Silicon Mac, QEMU TCG). Both reds are a peer-CPU kthread another oracle spins
up missing a microsecond-to-low-millisecond scheduling window under host CPU
pressure, and neither reads a wrong value on the property each oracle checks:

* Boot 5: `TEST:syscall:irq_hold_oracle` (#812's own oracle,
  `kernel/src/test_framework/registry.rs:5131`) --
  `[IRQ_HOLD_ORACLE:aarch64:attempts=3:armed=0:holder_cpu=1:irqs_enabled_before=1:masked_in_hold=1:sends=12:hold_us=12001:netrx_pending_at_release=1:received=32:stalled=0:hold_done=1:joined=1:FAIL]`
  -- `armed=0` on the final of 3 retries: the peer kthread's own
  `IRQ_HOLD_ACTIVE` flag was not observed inside the driver's spin-wait
  window on any of the 3. `stalled=0` reads that the peer was not actually
  wedged, just late.
* Boot 19: `TEST:syscall:fcntl_pm_contention_oracle` (#796's own oracle) --
  `FAIL:fcntl contention oracle's peer released the process-manager lock on
  its safety deadline; the arming rendezvous did not complete` -- the peer's
  own safety timeout fired and released the lock rather than risk a hang.

A concurrent `qemu-system-x86_64 -smp 1 -machine pc,accel=tcg` process from an
unrelated worktree was running on the same Mac for this run's own window;
`uptime` sampled between this run and the next read `load averages: 6.02 7.31
7.22` against this gate's own `load_at_start` readings of 4-8 in the next run,
taken once that process's load had visibly dropped, which came back 20/20.

## Rate

2 reds in this 1 run of 20 boots. A third, unrelated red in the PRECEDING run
of 20 (`tty_irq_fg_oracle`'s own entry-latency ceiling, #822's own oracle,
property held) shares the same peer-scheduling shape and is documented
alongside these two in
`docs/planning/green-program/irq-locks/822-TTY-IRQ-FG-2026-09-06.md`'s Landing
re-smoke section, where the 3 of 3 reds this landing hit (across the 2
non-clean runs of the 3 taken) are disclosed with their own serial excerpts.

## What this is not

Not #826: that signature is `Exec smoke did not complete` with 0 `EXEC_SMOKE`
lines in the serial at all -- a different oracle family, a different failure
shape. This issue is scoped to the peer-CPU arm/rendezvous-window class that
`irq_hold_oracle` and `fcntl_pm_contention_oracle` both show under host
pressure.

## Serials

`docs/planning/green-program/irq-locks/serials/822/23b-a64-strict-gate-run2-RED.txt`
(the full run), `23b-boot5-oracle-excerpt.txt`, `23b-boot19-oracle-excerpt.txt`,
and the host-load sample at `23-host-load-evidence.txt`.
title: aarch64 strict gate: irq_hold_oracle/fcntl_pm_contention_oracle miss their arm/rendezvous window under host CPU pressure
